components.name: Primary Download Button
components.description: The canonical release action in mint.
components.html: Download latest APK

components.name: Secondary Source Button
components.description: A quiet bordered action paired with the primary release action.
components.css: .ds-source{min-width:230px;min-height:56px;padding:0 20px;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:1px solid var(--line,#2c3953);border-radius:12px;background:transparent;color:var(--white,#f7f9fc);font:600 17px/1.55 'Golos Text','Segoe UI',sans-serif;text-decoration:none;transition:background 180ms ease,border-color 180ms ease,transform 400ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)}.ds-source:hover{border-color:var(--fog,#aab5c8);background:var(--panel,#11182a);transform:translateY(-3px)}.ds-source:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--coral,#ff8d7f);outline-offset:4px}

components.name: Mode Switch
components.description: A two-state transcription selector with semantically distinct signal colors.
components.css: .ds-modes{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;padding:4px;border:1px solid var(--line,#2c3953);border-radius:13px;background:var(--ink,#0b1020)}.ds-modes button{min-height:46px;padding:0 12px;border:0;border-radius:9px;background:transparent;color:var(--fog,#aab5c8);font:400 11px/1.55 'SFMono-Regular','Cascadia Code','Roboto Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:.05em;text-transform:uppercase;cursor:pointer;transition:color 180ms ease,background 180ms ease}.ds-modes button[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--mint,#7de4c4);color:var(--ink-deep,#070b16);font-weight:700}.ds-modes button[data-accurate][aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--coral,#ff8d7f)}.ds-modes button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--coral,#ff8d7f);outline-offset:4px}

components.name: Live Dictation Field
components.description: The signature field showing cumulative transcript insertion and live status.
components.html:
Focused text fieldReady
Move the release to Friday morning and add the APK link.
components.css: .ds-field{min-height:190px;padding:25px 92px 30px 28px;border:1px solid var(--line,#2c3953);border-radius:16px;background:var(--panel,#11182a);color:var(--white,#f7f9fc)}.ds-field-meta{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:20px;color:var(--fog,#aab5c8);font:400 11px/1.55 'SFMono-Regular','Cascadia Code','Roboto Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase}.ds-ready{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;color:var(--mint,#7de4c4)}.ds-ready i{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;background:currentColor}.ds-transcript{margin-top:34px;font:500 clamp(22px,2.55vw,38px)/1.32 'Golos Text','Segoe UI',sans-serif;letter-spacing:-.025em}.ds-caret{display:inline-block;width:2px;height:1em;margin-left:4px;background:var(--mint,#7de4c4);vertical-align:-.12em;animation:ds-blink 900ms step-end infinite}@keyframes ds-blink{0%,45%{opacity:1}46%,100%{opacity:0}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-caret{animation-duration:1ms;animation-iteration-count:1}}

components.name: Microphone Signal
components.description: The circular five-bar action that changes from mint to coral while listening.
components.css: .ds-mic{width:68px;height:68px;padding:0;display:grid;place-items:center;border:0;border-radius:50%;background:var(--mint,#7de4c4);color:var(--ink,#0b1020);cursor:pointer;transition:background 180ms ease,transform 400ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)}.ds-mic span{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:3px}.ds-mic i{width:3px;height:20px;border-radius:3px;background:currentColor}.ds-mic i:nth-child(1),.ds-mic i:nth-child(5){transform:scaleY(.3)}.ds-mic i:nth-child(2),.ds-mic i:nth-child(4){transform:scaleY(.65)}.ds-mic:hover{background:var(--mint-hover,#9aefd5);transform:translateY(-3px)}.ds-mic:active{transform:translateY(1px) scale(.97)}.ds-mic:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--coral,#ff8d7f);outline-offset:4px}

narrative.overview:
OpenDictate presents speech as a precise, observable input process rather than an abstract AI effect. Deep navy surfaces, hairline structure, compact instrument labels, a live caret, and the five-bar waveform make the interface feel focused, technical, and calm. Mint carries the active voice signal; coral appears only when a mode or state needs meaningful contrast.

This file is the repository-wide authority for web and public brand surfaces. The Android app shares the navy–mint–coral character, but its current Compose palette intentionally differs at several values and its controls, typography scale, insets, motion, and 48 dp touch targets remain Material 3-native. Do not mechanically transplant web pixels or fonts into Android.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy work surfaces with no light-theme inversion.
Mint waveform geometry and caret behavior as the signature motif.
Restrained coral reserved for Accurate/listening contrast and focus.
Unbounded display statements, Golos body copy, and monospaced utility labels.
Hairline ledgers and routes instead of floating marketing cards.
Direct, literal diagrams and interactions instead of decorative product mockups.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Mint means live, primary, or device-side activity; coral means a deliberate alternate mode, active replay, or focus. Never decorate with both indiscriminately.

rules.name: The Dark-Only Rule
rules.body: Web and brand surfaces are authored as a true dark scheme, not as colors awaiting automatic inversion.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Unbounded states the proposition, Golos explains it, and mono labels the instrument. Do not swap their jobs.

rules.name: The Working-Surface Rule
rules.body: Organize information as one continuous instrument panel separated by rules; do not replace the ledger with a generic feature-card mosaic.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface earns separation through tone and structure. Never add ambient card shadows or glass effects.

rules.name: The Shape-Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Curves belong to touchable controls and live signal geometry. Content organization remains rectilinear and ruled.

dos: Do make the waveform, caret, route lines, and state labels explain how speech reaches text.
Do use hairline structure and tonal layers to organize dense information.
Do preserve the bilingual Latin/Cyrillic font setup and responsive English/Russian copy behavior.
Do keep every web control keyboard-visible and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Do theme Android through Material 3 roles and components while retaining its existing Compose palette and 48 dp minimum targets.
donts: Don't introduce generic feature-card grids, detached phone mockups, stock AI imagery, gradients, glassmorphism, or ambient shadows.
Don't use coral as routine decoration or let it compete with mint for the primary action.
Don't replace Unbounded headlines with default sans type or use Unbounded for paragraphs.
Don't flatten desktop composition onto mobile; preserve the explicit 1040px and 700px reflows.
Don't copy web pixel values, web fonts, or hover-only affordances directly into native Android UI.
